Subject: CentraPay redlines (MSA + Order Form) — forum & injunctive relief

Vanessa,

Thanks for the call yesterday — attaching our initial redlines for the MSA and the Order Form. High level: CentraPay can accept most commercial terms but we need clarity on two narrow but material items before legal signs off: choice of law/forum and interim relief for IP/data misuse.

Specific asks from our side:
- Choice of law: prefer New York law for the MSA (we're a NY-headquartered entity).
- Forum: want exclusive venue in NY state courts; however we are open to arbitration for non-injunctive disputes if Redwood is agreeable.
- Interim/injunctive relief: request an explicit carveout allowing CentraPay to seek emergency court relief (injunctive relief, attachment) in NY courts without breaching an arbitration requirement.

We've attached CentraPay_Redlines_v1.pdf with markups. We'd like to get this wrapped this week to keep the Q4 go-live timeline.

Can you confirm who on your side will own the negotiation on the legal language? If there are two viable pathways (NY courts or arbitration with carveout for interim relief), happy to evaluate your proposed drafting.

Thanks,
Samantha Morris\Legal Counsel\CentraPay
Attachment: CentraPay_Redlines_v1.pdf

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CentraPay redlines (MSA + Order Form) — forum & injunctive relief

Samantha — thanks for sharing and for the clear asks. Looping in Laura (legal) and Jonas (sales ops) to align.

Quick thoughts:
- We can be flexible on governing law. Main risk is multi-jurisdiction discovery and mounting costs if forum is outside CA; historically, NY governing law with US-court-only venue has been a sticking point for some RD customers but we can work options.
- On arbitration: Redwood favors arbitration for expedited resolution, but we acknowledge interim relief carveouts are standard — Redwood is typically fine with an express injunctive-relief exception to arbitration.

Laura / Jonas — propose we provide CentraPay two drafting options:
Option A (NY courts): MSA governed by NY law; exclusive venue in state and federal courts located in New York County; no arbitration. Includes explicit interim relief language so either party can seek emergency relief.
Option B (Arbitration + carveout): Governing law NY; disputes subject to binding arbitration (JAMS/AAA), but carve out interim equitable relief allowing either party to apply to a US court for injunctive or other provisional relief, limited to preservation and immediate harm (brief, narrowly tailored). Arbitration would remain for the merits.

I'll draft brief inline language for both options and send over in a follow-up. We can also propose a monetary threshold for arbitration-exemption (e.g., claims < $50k go to small claims) if it helps.

Timelines: we can put language to you tomorrow, and ask for a counter within 48 hours to hit your week goal.

Thanks — V

Attachment: proposed_clause_options.docx

Subject: RE: CentraPay redlines (MSA + Order Form) — forum & injunctive relief

Vanessa / Jonas / Samantha — see below the two redline-ready clauses (clean & redline text included in attached doc). My recommendation is Option B (arbitration + narrow interim relief carveout) because it preserves Redwood's arbitration preference while meeting CentraPay's need for emergency court access. Option B also reduces cross-border enforcement friction.

Option A (NY courts — client-preferred):
Governing Law: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York without regard to conflict of laws principles.
Venue: Each party hereby consents to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement.

Option B (Arbitration + interim relief carveout — recommended):
Governing Law: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York without regard to conflict of laws principles.
Dispute Resolution: Except as set forth below, any dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be finally resolved by binding arbitration administered by JAMS in San Francisco, California, under JAMS Comprehensive Arbitration Rules and Procedures.
Interim Relief: Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may, without waiving the right to compel arbitration, seek from any state or federal court in the United States interim or provisional relief, including injunctive relief, attachment, or other equitable relief, solely to preserve the status quo or prevent immediate and irreparable harm. Any request for interim relief shall be narrowly tailored to the relief sought and, unless the court orders otherwise, shall not determine the merits of the dispute.

Other drafting points:
- Limit jurisdictional carveout to US courts (helps avoid parallel foreign litigation).
- Add a clause stating that the party seeking interim relief must promptly notify the other and file for arbitration within 30 days of seeking interim relief.
- Consider a PTO-style escalation: if emergency relief is granted, the parties proceed to expedited arbitration with a shortened discovery track.

I've attached redline_MSA_legaltrack.docx with inline changes. If CentraPay prefers Option A, Redwood legal will accept but would like to include a mutual forum-selection clause (both parties in NY) and a waiver of class/collective actions.

Laura Bennett\Senior Counsel, Contracts\Redwood Inference
